settings.label: Chains
settings.why: empty takes every chain in the file

settings.label: Hotspots
settings.why: residue numbers of this structure, as 54,56,66-70 or A54,B12-16. Needed by the cards that aim at a site, which here is the design tools. A folded structure is numbered by the sequence it was folded from, so 54 is its 54th residue and the chains are named from A

settings.label: Shortest binder
settings.why: how many residues, at the shortest

settings.label: Longest binder

cards.name: Structure file
cards.tagline: a structure you already have, on the cluster
cards.note: The structure as it stands, for the cards below to prepare and simulate. Everything in the file is handed on and prepared as one molecule: where a file holds a receptor and a separate partner that have to be prepared apart from each other, say so on the target card instead, which is the card that names chains.

settings.label: Structure file
settings.why: a PDB or mmCIF file on the cluster. It is copied into the flow's own inputs as the flow starts, so every card below reads one file in one place - and tidying the folder it came from later cannot take the structure of a finished flow with it

cards.name: Boltz-2
cards.tagline: fold a sequence, or co-fold a complex
cards.note: One sequence folds one structure, for a target card to take. Fill in a second sequence and the two are folded together as a complex - a receptor with the DNA, RNA or peptide that binds it - which goes on to be prepared and simulated. A structure of more chains than five is a job for the Boltz-2 page.

settings.label: Sequence
settings.why: one chain, in one-letter codes. Case does not matter - neither tool makes the distinction, so a sequence pasted in lower case is read as upper - but a letter that is not a residue does, and is refused here rather than folded as nothing

ligand.label: Ligand
ligand.placeholder: a CCD code, for example HEM or ATP
ligand.why: one small molecule, by its Chemical Component Dictionary code. The common ones are listed on the Boltz-2 page, and any code this install has a component for is taken here

ion.label: Ion
ion.placeholder: a CCD code, for example MN, FE, CU or ZN
ion.why: one ion, by its Chemical Component Dictionary code. Several of the same ion are copies of this row rather than a row each

ccd.label: CCD code
ccd.placeholder: a code, for example FE2 or HEM
ccd.why: any component in the Chemical Component Dictionary, by its code. This is the row for one the ion and ligand lists have not got: ferrous iron is FE2, and those lists carry FE, which is ferric

smiles.label: SMILES
smiles.why: one small molecule as SMILES. Boltz-2 reads it with RDKit and standardizes it itself, so it is taken as written

settings.label: What it is
settings.why: the alphabet the sequence is checked against, and the model used for it

settings.label: Copies
settings.why: more than one folds a homo-oligomer: the same sequence again as chains A, B, C

settings.label: Modified residues
settings.why: as 12 SEP, 40 TPO: the residue's position in the sequence above and the code it becomes. A code that is not a modification of that residue is refused as the flow is queued

settings.label: Alignments
settings.why: fetch asks the alignment server for one per protein chain while the flow is being queued, on the login node, which is the only place that can reach it. single folds from the sequence alone: nothing is fetched, and both the structure and its confidence fall away - measured here, a complex scoring 0.80 fell to about 0.12, far enough that a wrong answer can outscore the right one. Choose it to see a shape, never to rank anything

notes.fetch: one alignment per protein chain, from the MSA server
notes.single: no alignment: much worse, and the confidence with it

settings.label: Recycling steps

settings.label: Sampling steps
settings.why: steps in the diffusion. 200 is Boltz-2's own

settings.label: Seed

settings.placeholder: no seeding, which is Boltz-2's own

settings.label: Steering potentials
settings.why: off is Boltz-2's own. On is slower, and upstream reports structures that make better physical sense

settings.label: Card

settings.label: Walltime

cards.name: RFdiffusion
cards.tagline: design a binder backbone, then its sequence
cards.note: Designs come out placed on the target, so they go straight on to be prepared and simulated.

settings.label: Backbones to generate
settings.why: each is a separate diffusion, and the whole run is this many

settings.label: Sequences per backbone
settings.why: ProteinMPNN designs this many for each backbone, and the best is kept

settings.label: GPU
settings.why: auto takes the largest GPU this cluster has

settings.label: Noise scale
settings.why: 0 is what the binder-design example uses, and is a real answer rather than an empty one. Higher is more varied and fewer of them fold

settings.label: Diffusion steps
settings.why: fewer is faster and rougher, and RFdiffusion itself asserts at least 15

settings.label: Checkpoint
settings.why: empty takes the binder-design default

notes: Complex_base, which is what RFdiffusion picks itself once hotspots are given
notes.Complex_beta_ckpt.pt: the beta complex model: more varied binders, and fewer of them hold up

settings.label: Noise schedule
settings.why: constant holds the noise where it is set; linear walks it to the figure below over the run

notes.constant: the one scale, every step. RFdiffusion's own default
notes.linear: from the scale above at the first step to the one below at the last

settings.label: Final noise scale
settings.why: where the linear schedule ends up

constant.why: not read on a constant schedule, which holds the noise scale above all the way through

settings.label: Pull on the design
settings.why: a force on the binder while it diffuses. Empty is what the binder-design example uses, and RFdiffusion's own notes say these sit badly with hotspots: start without one

notes: none, as RFdiffusion's own default is
notes.binder_ROG: pulls the binder compact, by its radius of gyration
notes.interface_ncontacts: more contacts between the binder and the target

settings.label: How hard it pulls
settings.why: 1 is each potential's own weight

cases.why: not read until a pull is chosen above

settings.label: Guide scale
settings.why: how much of the pull reaches the diffusion; 10 is RFdiffusion's own

cases.why: not read until a pull is chosen above

settings.label: Guide decay
settings.why: how the pull fades as the structure settles

notes.constant: the same at every step. RFdiffusion's own default
notes.quadratic: fades faster, so late steps are nearly free

cases.why: not read until a pull is chosen above

settings.label: Keep the diffusion trajectories
settings.why: two files per design showing every step, for looking at the diffusion itself

settings.label: Repeat the same designs
settings.why: seeds each design from its own number, so the same run made twice gives the same backbones

settings.label: ProteinMPNN model
settings.why: the figure is the backbone noise it was trained with, in hundredths of an angstrom

notes.v_48_002: 0.02 A: closest to the backbone it is given
notes.v_48_030: 0.30 A: most forgiving of a rough backbone

settings.label: Soluble ProteinMPNN
settings.why: weights trained on soluble proteins only, which is what a binder has to be

settings.label: Sequence temperature
settings.why: higher is more varied; ProteinMPNN suggests 0.1 to 0.3

settings.label: Sequence seed
settings.why: 0 picks a new one each run; any other number gives the same sequences again

settings.label: Excluded amino acids
settings.why: letters the designed sequence may not use, as C to keep cysteines out

settings.label: Backbone noise
settings.why: noise on the backbone while the sequence is designed; the released models were trained at up to 0.30 A

cards.name: RFdiffusion3
cards.tagline: design a binder, every atom at once
cards.note: Designs come out placed on the target, as RFdiffusion's do.

settings.label: Designs to generate
settings.why: generated together in one pass, so this costs GPU memory rather than time

settings.label: Sequences per design
settings.why: RFdiffusion3 writes a sequence of its own, and MPNN is still what the authors' own pipeline redesigns protein backbones with before ordering

settings.label: GPU
settings.why: auto takes the largest GPU this cluster has. An rtx is not offered: this model does not run on one

settings.label: Step scale
settings.why: the diversity knob. Higher is less varied and more of them hold up

settings.label: Diffusion steps
settings.why: fewer is faster and rougher

settings.label: Classifier-free guidance
settings.why: holds a design closer to what was asked of it. Off is the model's own default, and it is turned on for conditioning that must be obeyed

settings.label: How closely held
settings.why: 1.5 is the model's own; 1 is no guidance at all

false.why: not read until the guidance above is on

settings.label: Passes
settings.why: the run makes this many passes, so a campaign is the designs above times this

settings.label: Seed
settings.why: the same number gives the same designs again

settings.label: Noise scale
settings.why: the noise put back at each step; 0 takes it out altogether

settings.label: Churn
settings.why: how much each step is re-noised before it is denoised again; 0 samples the diffusion as a plain equation

settings.label: Cyclic peptide
settings.why: joins the binder's ends, which RFdiffusion3 takes for one designed chain

settings.label: Fewer loops
settings.why: asks for a binder with less loop in it, which is the one that folds

cards.name: RFD4-Proteina
cards.tagline: design to what has to be in the right place
cards.note: Designs come out placed on the target, as the other design cards' do. Nothing here scores them: fold them to rank them.

settings.label: Designs to generate
settings.why: replicates of the same design problem, so this costs time rather than GPU memory

settings.label: GPU
settings.why: auto takes the largest GPU this cluster has. An rtx is not offered: this model does not run on one

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: the model loads in the first few minutes of it. A job that ends early is charged for what it used, so round up rather than cut it fine

settings.label: Sampling steps
settings.why: fewer is faster and rougher; 60 is the model's own

settings.label: Recycling
settings.why: how much the model reconsiders its own answer as it goes. These are its own presets for designing a protein against a protein

notes.medium/front_loaded: 180, which the model's own validation uses for this task
notes.high/front_loaded: 300: the most thorough, and the slowest

settings.label: Designs per batch
settings.why: generated together on the GPU. The tool's own advice is to try your longest input at 1 first

settings.label: Compile the model first
settings.why: a warm-up costing minutes that makes every design after it faster: worth it over a campaign, not over a handful

settings.label: Seed
settings.why: the same number gives the same designs again

settings.label: Fold and rank designs
settings.why: Boltz-2 folds each design from its sequence alone and the result is measured onto the design: under about 2 A at pLDDT 70 the sequence folds into the shape it was designed for. Adds about 20 minutes to the same job

settings.label: Hold the target's shape
settings.why: its backbone keeps its geometry and its side chains stay free, so the binder is not designed to mimic them (C_CRDGRP)

settings.label: Show the target's sequence
settings.why: the model knows which residues it is designing against, not only where they are (C_SEQ)

settings.label: Reach the site
settings.why: off, the condition naming the marked residues is left out of the spec and the model is not told to reach them (C_HOT)

cards.name: BoltzGen
cards.tagline: generate a binder against the target
cards.note: Generates binders against a protein target and leaves them already placed on it. The small-molecule protocol needs a ligand a flow does not carry, and is refused.

settings.label: What to design
settings.why: the model's own protocols; the binder kind is chosen here

notes.peptide-anything: a short peptide, cysteine-free by default
notes.protein-small_molecule: needs the target's ligand, which a flow has taken out of the receptor before this card; it is refused rather than run without it
notes.protein-redesign: the binder already on the target, designed again

settings.label: Designs to generate
settings.why: BoltzGen is built to generate many and keep the best few, which is the box below

settings.label: Designs to keep
settings.why: the filtering stage picks this many out of the designs above, spread for variety rather than taking the top of one list

settings.label: GPU
settings.why: BoltzGen needs 40 GB or more; the smaller GPUs run out

settings.label: Cyclic peptide
settings.why: peptide protocols only

settings.label: Step scale
settings.why: it scales the diffusion step, and is not a count of steps

settings.label: Noise scale
settings.why: a fixed noise scale instead of the schedule BoltzGen would use

settings.label: Fold and score designs
settings.why: the ranking comes from this; off leaves designs unranked

settings.label: Sequences per design
settings.why: BoltzGen's inverse folding writes this many for each backbone

settings.label: Excluded amino acids
settings.why: letters the sequences may not use. This replaces the protocol's own list, and the peptide, nanobody and antibody protocols leave cysteine out: keep the C in

settings.label: Coldspots
settings.why: residues the binder should keep clear of; BoltzGen is told they are not binding, the opposite of a hotspot

settings.label: Quality against variety
settings.why: 0 picks the best designs, 1 the most different ones

settings.label: Drop lopsided sequences
settings.why: takes out designs made mostly of alanine, glycine, glutamate, leucine or valine. On is BoltzGen's own default

settings.label: Model
settings.why: BoltzGen ships two design models and uses both by default, half the designs each

notes.both: half the designs from each. BoltzGen's own default
notes.adherence: designs that stick closer to what was asked

cards.name: Prepare
cards.tagline: prepare the receptor and the partner each on its own, then rejoin them
cards.note: Put in by the canvas on every link that carries a structure into the simulation, and part of that link rather than a card of its own: it splits what arrives into the receptor and the partner, prepares each on its own - protonation at the pH above, termini, disulfides, gaps - puts them back together and checks the net charge. A side of several chains is prepared whole, so the bonds between its chains are kept. What it decided is listed on the card when it has run.

settings.label: pH
settings.why: every molecule is protonated at this pH, and one flow has one pH

notes.propka: pdb2pqr with propka at the pH above: each titratable residue gets the state its own surroundings call for
notes.pdbfixer: PDBFixer's rules at the pH above, which are the standard states and no more
notes.none: the hydrogens in the file, or the engine's own defaults where there are none

settings.label: Longest gap to model, residues
settings.why: a gap inside a chain up to this long, found from the sequence the file records, is built, relaxed and its joins checked; a longer one is left open and its two ends capped (Cap the breaks). 12 at most, 0 builds none, and a chain's missing ends are never built

settings.label: Trim predicted tails below pLDDT
settings.why: for a predicted model: terminal residues under this confidence are trimmed; 0 keeps every one, and a structure with no pLDDT in it is untouched

settings.label: Alternate location to keep
settings.why: a crystal structure that models two positions for a side chain keeps this one; the atoms of the others are dropped

settings.label: Model to take
settings.why: for an NMR ensemble or any multi-model file: which model is prepared. The first unless you say otherwise

settings.label: Crystal waters
settings.why: for the simulation

notes.far: keep those within 5 Å of the partner

settings.label: Keep metals and cofactors
settings.why: into the simulation they ride through at their own coordinates, and it listed as dropped

settings.label: Drop the crystallization buffers
settings.why: glycerol, sulfate, PEG, acetate, DMSO and the rest of what the crystallographer added; off, each one has to be covered by a force field or the run is refused by name

settings.label: Keep the hetero groups that are neither
settings.why: a group that is not a buffer, a metal or a known cofactor: kept only if a force field here covers it, and named in the refusal if not

settings.label: Also drop, by residue name
settings.why: residue names dropped whatever their class, separated by commas: NAD, HEM. This is what a refusal naming a group it cannot cover asks for

settings.label: Cap the breaks
settings.why: a gap left open has its two ends capped, an NME on the residue before it and an ACE on the residue after it, so neither is a charged terminus the protein does not have; the chain's own termini stay charged. Off, each piece ends in charged termini, an OXT before the gap and NH3+ after it

settings.label: Minimize each molecule
settings.why: restrained, in vacuum: it takes the clashes out and moves nothing else

settings.label: Minimization steps
settings.why: L-BFGS steps on each molecule; 0 skips the minimization as surely as the switch above

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Minimization restraint, kcal/mol/Å²
settings.why: held on the heavy atoms the file already had, so only the modeled residues move; 0 lets everything move

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Minimize in implicit solvent
settings.why: GBn2 instead of vacuum: a better answer for a modeled loop, and about ten times slower

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Walltime

cards.name: Prepare receptor
cards.tagline: prepare the target's receptor once, for the docking
cards.note: Put in by the canvas between a target and every docking card it feeds, once per target: the target's chains alone, through HOPE-MD's Prepare - protonation at the flow's pH, AMBER names, termini and breaks, gaps up to the length above built back from the sequence the file records - with the waters and hetero groups dropped, except the ions the docking can use. The hotspots are checked against what comes out: one on a built residue is flagged on the card, and one that is missing stops the docking, by name.

settings.label: pH
settings.why: the receptor is protonated at this pH, and one flow has one pH

notes.propka: pdb2pqr with propka at the pH above: each titratable residue gets the state its own surroundings call for
notes.pdbfixer: PDBFixer's rules at the pH above, which are the standard states and no more
notes.none: the hydrogens in the file, or the engine's own defaults where there are none

settings.label: Longest gap to model, residues
settings.why: a gap inside a chain up to this long, found from the sequence the file records, is built, relaxed and its joins checked; a longer one is left open and its two ends capped (Cap the breaks). 12 at most, 0 builds none, and a chain's missing ends are never built

settings.label: Trim predicted tails below pLDDT
settings.why: for a predicted model: terminal residues under this confidence are trimmed; 0 keeps every one, and a structure with no pLDDT in it is untouched

settings.label: Alternate location to keep
settings.why: a crystal structure that models two positions for a side chain keeps this one; the atoms of the others are dropped

settings.label: Model to take
settings.why: for an NMR ensemble or any multi-model file: which model is prepared. The first unless you say otherwise

settings.label: Cap the breaks
settings.why: a gap left open has its two ends capped, an NME on the residue before it and an ACE on the residue after it, so neither is a charged terminus the protein does not have; the chain's own termini stay charged. Off, each piece ends in charged termini, an OXT before the gap and NH3+ after it

settings.label: Minimize each molecule
settings.why: restrained, in vacuum: it takes the clashes out and moves nothing else

settings.label: Minimization steps
settings.why: L-BFGS steps on each molecule; 0 skips the minimization as surely as the switch above

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Minimization restraint, kcal/mol/Å²
settings.why: held on the heavy atoms the file already had, so only the modeled residues move; 0 lets everything move

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Minimize in implicit solvent
settings.why: GBn2 instead of vacuum: a better answer for a modeled loop, and about ten times slower

false.why: not read: the minimization is off

settings.label: Which of what arrives to simulate

notes.rank: the best few, by the score the tool that made them gave them, ranked across all of its partners together
notes.name: the ones named below, whatever their rank

settings.label: Simulate the best of what arrives
settings.why: per track, best score first across all of that track's partners. Each one is a full simulation, so this is what the flow costs

name.why: not read: the structures named below are the ones simulated

settings.label: Structures to simulate, by name
settings.why: as the preparation named them, separated by commas
settings.placeholder: not read: the best few are taken by rank

name.why: the names as they arrive here, separated by commas: a fold's are <card>_model<n>. A name nothing answers to is said before anything is queued

settings.label: Settings for one structure
settings.why: a group per structure, as name: key=value, key=value, with a semicolon between groups. The keys are this card's own, so "3cc1_cluster2: length_ns=200, engine=openmm" runs that one structure for longer on another engine and leaves the rest alone. A value that is itself a list, as the restrained residues are, is separated by spaces here, because the commas separate the settings
settings.placeholder: every run takes the settings on this card

settings.label: Poses per peptide
settings.why: the best few poses of each partner, not only its first; the best of what arrives still caps the whole

settings.label: Engine
settings.why: the same system on any of the five; Amber is the fastest here and what the lab's benchmarks are in

notes.amber: pmemd.cuda: the fastest on these cards, and the engine the lab's timings are measured on
notes.openmm: a Python engine on the same Amber topology
notes.gromacs: the Amber topology converted by ParmEd
notes.namd: NAMD 3, reading the prmtop itself; no four-site water
notes.desmond: Schrödinger's, with its own OPLS force field and box

notes.water: a periodic water box around the complex
notes.membrane: a lipid bilayer, with water above and below it. The force field, the water, the box shape and the salt follow the bilayer build and are written for you

settings.label: Length, ns
settings.why: production, per replicate; past the queue's limit it is chained as segments

cpu.why: a CPU check is at most 10 ns: it answers whether the pose holds at the start, not how it behaves

settings.label: Frames to keep
settings.why: over the whole production, so the interval is the length divided by this: 5000 of 100 ns is one every 20 ps, which is HOPE-MD's own. It has to be a whole number of steps and no longer than the 200 ps MM-GBSA takes its frames at, and the canvas says which number to type instead

cpu.why: a CPU check keeps at most 500 frames

settings.label: Replicates
settings.why: independent repeats, each with its own seed; 5 is the most HOPE-MD runs

settings.label: Binding energy by MM-GBSA
settings.why: GB-Neck2 over the frames below, per replicate: the number a flow is usually drawn to get. Off for a run of one molecule, which has no interface

settings.label: Lipid
settings.why: the bilayer is tiled from a pre-equilibrated patch of this lipid

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

desmond.why: Desmond's System Builder ships POPC, POPE, DPPC, DMPC bilayers

settings.label: Water above and below the bilayer, Å
settings.why: under 5 Å the head groups see their own image, over 40 Å is water for nothing

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

settings.why: where the middle of the bilayer sits; 0 is the OPM convention and what an oriented structure expects

notes.annotation: orient on the transmembrane segments, from the ones typed below or the ones UniProt annotates

settings.label: Transmembrane segments
settings.why: as chain:start-end, separated by commas: A:30-56, A:71-96. Typed ones are used in place of whatever was found

water.why: not read: the run is in a water box

notes.compact: a truncated octahedron: the fewest waters for the same minimum image distance, and the default
notes.cubic: a cube, for comparison with work that used one
notes.rectangular: an orthorhombic box, which is what a bilayer takes

desmond.why: Desmond's System Builder builds an orthorhombic box whatever is asked

membrane.why: a bilayer is periodic in x and y, so the box is rectangular

settings.label: Padding, Å
settings.why: water between the solute and the box edge; under the 10 Å cutoff the complex sees its own periodic image

membrane.why: not read: a bilayer's water is the padding above and below it

settings.label: Salt
settings.why: the box is neutralized first, then brought to the concentration below

notes.KCl: for work done in potassium buffer
notes.MgCl2: for a nucleic acid, which binds Mg2+; not for a bilayer, which takes a monovalent pair

membrane.why: a bilayer build places a monovalent pair: NaCl or KCl

settings.label: Salt concentration, mM
settings.why: 150 mM is physiological. It is also the salt MM-GBSA is computed at, so it changes the binding energy as well as the box

settings.label: Residues held still in production
settings.why: as 54,56,66-70 or A54,B12-16, in the numbering the preparation kept. For a run meant to answer what the rest does while these stay put
settings.placeholder: nothing is held: the whole complex is free

settings.label: Production restraint, kcal/mol/Å²
settings.why: how hard those residues are held, and the first rung of the equilibration ladder either way

cases.why: the first rung of the equilibration ladder; no residue is held in production

settings.label: Score from, ns
settings.why: skip the start, where the complex is still settling; 0 scores from the first frame

settings.label: Score to, ns
settings.why: empty scores to the end

settings.label: Score every, ps
settings.why: how often a frame of that window is scored; it can be no finer than the interval the frames above are kept at

settings.label: Write each run's report when it finishes
settings.why: the run's own report, as the Runs screen would write it: one job per run, behind the simulation

settings.label: Make each run's videos when it finishes
settings.why: a job of its own per run, cut from the trajectory

settings.label: Tidy each run when it finishes
settings.why: a last job packs away the small files a finished run no longer needs; the results still load. Off, a batch of runs is a great many files

settings.label: Frames the viewer shows, one in
settings.why: the trajectory the Results viewer loads is thinned by this, so 20 of the 5000 frames kept is 250 to scrub through

settings.label: Temperature, K
settings.why: the thermostat's target through heating, equilibration and production

settings.label: Pressure, bar
settings.why: the barostat's target once the box is equilibrated at constant pressure

settings.label: Timestep, fs
settings.why: 2 fs, or 4 fs with hydrogen mass repartitioning

desmond.why: Desmond runs its RESPA scheme: the timestep is fixed at 2 fs and there is no hydrogen mass repartitioning

settings.label: Equilibration, ps
settings.why: over the restraint ladder

settings.label: Heating, ps
settings.why: from 0 K to the temperature above, restrained, before the ladder

settings.label: Minimization steps
settings.why: on the built box, before any heating: it takes the clashes out of the solvation

settings.label: Random seed
settings.why: -1 lets each replicate pick its own

settings.label: Water
settings.why: empty takes what the force field was fitted to

notes: the force field's own pairing: OPC with ff19SB, TIP3P with ff14SB, SPC with Desmond's OPLS
notes.OPC: ff19SB's own, and not for NAMD or Desmond
notes.TIP4P-Ew: not for NAMD, which cannot run a four-site water from the Amber topology

membrane.why: a bilayer build has one water and it is written for you: TIP3P, or SPC on Desmond, whose lipid patches come hydrated with it

settings.label: Protein force field
settings.why: empty takes the engine's own: ff19SB on the four Amber-topology engines, OPLS_2005 on Desmond

notes.ff14SB: the same four, for comparison with older work
notes.OPLS_2005: Desmond, which types the whole system with its own OPLS

desmond.why: Desmond types the whole system with its own OPLS: OPLS_2005 or OPLS4

membrane.why: a bilayer build has one force field and it is written for you: ff14SB, which is the only one OpenMM ships lipid17 alongside, or Desmond's own OPLS

settings.label: DNA and RNA force field
settings.why: for a strand in the run; empty takes the engine's usual

notes.bsc1+OL3: any engine but Desmond, which types DNA and RNA with its own OPLS and takes no choice

notes.gpu: one card per replicate, which is how these engines are meant to be run
notes.cpu: one whole node, for a short check while the GPU queue is full: Amber or GROMACS, at most 10 ns and 500 frames

notes: the cluster's default, which on Grace is a100

cpu.why: not read: the run is on CPU

a100.why: a Grace a100 node has 2 cards

a40.why: a Grace a40 node has 3 cards

rtx.why: a Grace rtx node has 2 cards

settings.why: beside the card, for the parts that are not on it; a CPU check takes a whole node whatever this says

settings.label: Replicates running at once
settings.why: a throttle for a batch of runs against one allocation: empty queues them all and lets the cluster decide

cards.name: BioEmu
cards.tagline: sample the shapes one chain takes
cards.note: Samples the structures this chain takes, as a spread rather than one answer, and hands on the most populated of them. The alignment it needs is fetched while the flow is queued, on the login node, because a compute node here reaches no network at all. What comes out is not a trajectory: the shapes are independent draws from a distribution, so nothing below this card may read a rate or a pathway off them.

outputs.label: the shapes sampled, one structure each

settings.label: Sequence
settings.why: one protein chain, in one-letter codes. Case does not matter; a letter that is not one of the twenty amino acids does, and is refused here rather than sampled into something that means nothing

settings.label: Structures to sample
settings.why: a distribution, not a structure: ten says nothing about how wide it is. The cost is close to linear in this number

settings.label: Model
settings.why: v1.1 is what the paper reports, so it is what a number taken from a run can be compared against. Runs made on different checkpoints cannot be compared with one another

notes.bioemu-v1.1: the checkpoint of the published paper
notes.bioemu-v1.2: trained on more simulation and on measured folding free energies

settings.label: Shapes to hand on
settings.why: most populated first, each a structure the model drew. Whatever takes them prepares and simulates one run per shape, so this is what the rest of the flow costs

settings.label: Seed
settings.why: the same number gives the same samples again

settings.label: Card
settings.why: auto takes the largest card this cluster has. Sampling holds the whole chain on the card, so a long sequence wants the largest there is

settings.label: Walltime
settings.why: a few hundred samples of a small protein is minutes. A job killed at its walltime leaves nothing: the samples are written only once every batch has been drawn
